name: Dark Matter as Topological Defects in SL(6,C) Gauge Theory
description: Dark matter is not a new particle species but a geometric-topological phenomenon arising from Kibble-Zurek defect formation during the SL(6,C) → SU(6) phase transition in the early universe. The conjecture predicts Ω_DM / Ω_b ≈ 5 as a consequence of the homotopy group classification of defects in the symmetry-breaking pattern.
framework: SL(6,C) gauge theory with CGICE effective action

axioms.description: SL(6,C) is the gauge group of 6D spacetime prior to phase transition
The symmetry breaking pattern is SL(6,C) → SU(6) via CGICE mechanism
Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies: defect density ∝ τ_Q^{−ν/(1+νz)}
Homotopy groups: π₀(SU(6)) = 0, π₁(SU(6)) = 0, π₂(SU(6)) = 0, π₃(SU(6)) = ℤ
Topological defect energy density redshifts as ρ_defect ∝ a^{−3} (non-relativistic)
The ratio of defect to baryon density is set by the CGICE condensation scale Λ_CGICE / Λ_QCD
KLS constant λ_KLS = 35/3 for SL(6,C)/SU(6) symmetric space

claims.description: π₃ defect density predicts Ω_DM / Ω_b ≈ 5
Defect-stabilized galactic rotation curves match NFW profile
No new particles beyond Standard Model + sterile neutrino

targets.description: Prove Ω_DM / Ω_b = 5 from homotopy group classification + KZ mechanism
Derive NFW profile from CGICE topological defect density distribution
